citation.title: Equivariant neural operators for gradient-consistent topology optimization
citation.venue: Journal of Computational Design and Engineering 11(3), 91–100
citation.version_coded: published version; Cambridge Apollo repository copy

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The authors say neural operators substantially reduce solution time relative to classical numerical PDE solvers and use them to replace the solver in 3D SIMP.
claim.key_phrase: remarkable speed-ups over classical numerical PDE solvers
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 5.3 reports at least a fourfold inference speed improvement over classical SIMP; this is a lower bound, not an exact factor.
claim.alternatives: Abstract: the proposed U-Net FNO is said to outperform U-Net and other FNO methods (learned baselines; not the primary classical comparison). Section 5.3 reports at least fourfold inference improvement and gives an example at 160,000 voxels.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP with the classical finite-difference method (FDM) PDE solver
baseline.implementation: Classical SIMP with FDM; implementation details not stated
baseline.solver: FDM; iterative/direct solver details not stated
baseline.hardware_ml: Intel Xeon Silver 4210 CPU for inference (Table 2); GeForce RTX 2080 Ti GPU for training (Section 5.1)
baseline.problem_size: 3D, 39 × 39 × 4 voxel grid; also cites a 160,000-voxel fine grid (Sections 5.1, 5.3)
baseline.classical_iterations: SIMP trajectories run for 60 iterations in dataset construction (Section 5.1); stopping rule not stated
baseline.ml_time: 2–18 s average inference runtime across the listed NO variants (Table 2); less than 1 s for one NO solution at 160,000 voxels (Section 5.3)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; dataset contains almost 10,000 3D TO problems and is based on SIMP ground truths (Section 5.1)
baseline.quality_metric: intersection over union (IoU), failure percentage, mean compliance, and weighted mean absolute error (WMAE) against the reference SIMP trajectory (Section 5.2)
baseline.quality_gap: Quality and failure measures are reported by model and training-set size in Table 1; no explicit matched-quality tolerance is stated.

R1.evidence: Sections 5.2–5.3 and Tables 1–2 compare quality/failure measures and runtime, but do not specify a matched-quality tolerance or a classical stopping criterion for the speed comparison.

R2.evidence: Table 2 compares inference on the same Intel Xeon Silver 4210 CPU; text does not establish any other R2 criterion.

R3.evidence: Section 5.1 reports 2–14 h of training and training-set sizes; it does not report the cost of generating the SIMP training data or amortization.

R4.evidence: Sections 5.2–5.3 report quality/failure measures while SIMP is run with learned PDE solvers; no independent FDM/FE verification of the returned learned designs is stated.

reporting.n_test_cases: Not stated; all problems in the test dataset were evaluated (Section 5.2).

notes: The open access published version was read from the University of Cambridge Apollo repository. Section 5.1 says the study uses the SELTO disc dataset and cites DL4TO/NO libraries, but does not identify an experiment-specific public code release or its license.
